name: Pinnae Fistula or Cyst

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnosis of Pinnae Fistula or Cyst

criteria.description: Presence of a visible preauricular sinus or cyst opening anterior to the auricle
History of recurrent localized infections or discharge from the preauricular site
Ultrasound or MRI showing cystic or fistulous tract in the preauricular region

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a visible preauricular sinus or cyst opening with or without recurrent infections; imaging supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; imaging aids in surgical planning

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent purulent discharge from preauricular site

common.symptomName: Localized swelling anterior to the auricle

searchTerms: pain when touching area near ear

common.symptomName: Erythema around the sinus or cyst opening
Intermittent pain localized to the preauricular area

occasional.symptomName: Fistula tract extending into parotid gland tissue
searchTerms: abnormal tract extending into salivary gland

occasional.symptomName: Formation of abscess in preauricular region
Mild hearing impairment due to local inflammation
searchTerms: slight hearing difficulty due to swelling

rare.symptomName: Facial nerve palsy secondary to deep infection
searchTerms: paralysis of face due to deep infection

rare.symptomName: Chronic granulomatous inflammation of fistula tract
searchTerms: chronic inflammation with granulomas in fistula

rare.symptomName: Malignant transformation of cyst lining (very rare)

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers during infection episodes
Microbial culture of purulent discharge showing common skin flora or pathogens
imaging: Ultrasound demonstrating cystic lesion or fistulous tract
MRI delineating extent of fistula and involvement of adjacent structures
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; may be sporadic or familial
other: Physical examination revealing external sinus or cyst opening
Histopathology of excised cyst showing keratinizing squamous epithelium

distinguishingFeatures: Location along anterior border of sternocleidomastoid muscle
Typically presents as a painless mass without sinus tract

redFlags: Rapidly increasing swelling with severe pain
Signs of facial nerve weakness or palsy
Systemic signs of sepsis or deep neck infection
references: Orphanet: Pinnae Fistula or Cyst - ORPHA:155838
